newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg Q2 cereal volume up more than 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg Q2 cereal volume up more than 6 pct.

text.p: Kellogg Co said Friday its U.S. cereal sales volume rose more than six percent in the second quarter, contributing to strong overall results for the quarter.

Kellogg said earlier that its global sales volume in the second quarter gained 14 percent, including the Lender's Bagels business it acquired in December 1996. Excluding Lender's, volume was up eight percent.

"Our second quarter results were driven by cereal volume increases in all four of our global operating areas, continued double-digit volume growth in our convenience foods business, and savings from our ongoing cost-reduction initiatives," Arnold Langbo, chairman, said in a statement.
The four areas are North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia/Pacific.

Kellogg reported second quarter earnings of $0.83 a share before a $0.04 charge, far outpacing year-ago results of $0.45 and the First Call consensus of $0.73. It also beat second-quarter 1995 earnings of $0.77 a share.
Kellogg shares rose 4-1/4 at 96-1/8, after hitting a new 52-week high of 97-3/4.
